prs.title: perf(linter): disable papaya's `fast-barrier` to avoid a `membarrier` wait on Linux
prs.author: magurotuna
prs.body:
## Summary

On Linux, every `oxlint` run waits 20–40 ms when it creates its first papaya map. This PR removes the wait for both the CLI and the npm package by disabling `fast-barrier` feature of the papaya crate. It also adds a `cargo deny` rule that fails if any crate enables the feature again so we can notice it.

## Why it waits

With `fast-barrier`, `seize::Collector::new()` calls `membarrier(MEMBARRIER_CMD_REGISTER_PRIVATE_EXPEDITED)`. If the process already has more than one thread, the kernel waits for an RCU grace period before it returns ([kernel/sched/membarrier.c](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/v6.12/kernel/sched/membarrier.c#L442-L470)).

`oxc_linter` has one papaya map: [`modules_by_path`](crates/oxc_linter/src/service/runtime.rs#L59-L66), the module graph that the import plugin uses for rules across files, such as `import/no-cycle`. The map is a field of [`Runtime`](crates/oxc_linter/src/service/runtime.rs#L45), which holds the state of one lint run. [`LintService::new()`](crates/oxc_linter/src/service/mod.rs#L68-L71) creates the `Runtime` once per run. [`Runtime::new()`](crates/oxc_linter/src/service/runtime.rs#L208) first starts the rayon thread pool ([#L227](crates/oxc_linter/src/service/runtime.rs#L227)), and then it creates the map ([#L268](crates/oxc_linter/src/service/runtime.rs#L268)). So the main thread waits on every run. This happens even with the default config, which does not use the import plugin.

The npm package waits too. Creating the ma
…(truncated)

prs.title: refactor(ast)!: replace `StaticPropertyName`'s `Display` with `display()`
prs.author: Dunqing
prs.body:
`StaticPropertyName` implemented `Display`, so `.to_string()` turned a name into escaped text without saying so. That matters where the text is used as a key rather than shown. It now has a `display()` adapter like `JSStr`'s, so each caller says what it wants. Both `display()` docs now note that the output is not injective (`"\uD800"` and `"\\ud800"` print the same), so it must not be compared or used as a key.

The 31 current callers keep their output: they format diagnostics or messages, and the few that key by the text get the same keys as before.

**Breaking:** `StaticPropertyName` no longer implements `Display`. Use `name.display()`.

Came up in the review of rolldown/rolldown#11228. Part of #26242.

Implemented with AI assistance.

prs.title: fix(transformer)!: decode JSX entities to lone surrogates
prs.author: Dunqing
prs.body:
JSX numeric character references can name lone surrogates, as in `�`. They are now decoded with `JSStrBuilder`, so the JSX transform and the React Compiler keep lone surrogates, and adjacent references that form a pair join into one character. Generated JSX attributes that contain a lone surrogate are printed as JavaScript string expressions.

Both now share one decoder that follows Babel: only lowercase `&#x` is hexadecimal, and signed references such as `&#+65;` stay text. The React Compiler therefore keeps `A` as text instead of decoding it to `A`, like Babel and the JSX transform.

## Breaking changes

- `oxc_syntax::xml_entities::decode_entities` accumulates into a `JSStrBuilder`, and the new `decode_entity` returns a `JSChar`.

Part of #26242.

Implemented with AI assistance.

prs.title: fix(linter): search string values without UTF-8 conversion
prs.author: Dunqing
prs.body:
A lone surrogate anywhere in a string made `as_str()` return `None`, so rules skipped checks on ordinary text elsewhere in the value. For example, `test(" \uD800 my title ", () => {})` got no leading/trailing-space diagnostic.

This adds `contains`, `starts_with`, `ends_with`, `find` and `rfind` to `JSStr`. They take a `&str`, a `char` or a predicate, search the WTF-8 bytes without converting or allocating, and never match a lone surrogate with a character pattern. Seven linter rules and the formatter's JSX attribute checks use them. Lowercase-title fixes now check the source spelling, so an escaped first letter is reported without a fix.

Based on #26712. Part of #26242.

Implemented with AI assistance.

prs.body: Skip invalid spec like `printWidth: Infinity`.

prs.title: fix(linter): check module specifiers and string values that contain lone surrogates
prs.author: Dunqing
prs.body:
Lone surrogates disabled several lint checks and could count as allow-list matches. Module specifiers, names, whitespace and duplicate keys are now checked on the `JSStr` value. Fixes that need UTF-8 text keep the diagnostic and skip the fix.

User-configured regexes and globs only match UTF-8 text, so a value with a lone surrogate matches none of them. Allow-lists in `new-cap`, `no-unassigned-import`, `no-require-imports`, `no-large-snapshots` and `prop-name-casing` don't exempt it, `no-restricted-imports` and `valid-title` don't report it, and `valid-title`'s `mustMatch` does. `img-redundant-alt` searches the value's bytes directly. `import/extensions` (for `require()`) and `relative-url-style` still skip such values, as do static imports, because module records omit them.

`no-require-imports` now matches `allow` against a template's cooked value, and only when the template has no expressions, like typescript-eslint. The TypeScript `rewriteImportExtensions` option also rewrites specifiers that contain a lone surrogate.

Based on #26716. Part of #26242.

Implemented with AI assistance.

prs.title: fix(minifier): fold string indices by UTF-16 code unit
prs.author: Dunqing
prs.body:
String indexing now folds by UTF-16 code unit, so `"😀"[0]` folds to `"\uD83D"` and `"a\uD800b"[1]` to `"\uD800"`. The result is built with `JSStrBuilder` instead of a temporary heap string; ordinary strings keep the native UTF-8 path.

Closes #26636. Based on #26717. Part of #26242. Continues #26752.

Implemented with AI assistance.

prs.title: refactor(linter/eslint/no-restricted-imports): remove use of `unreachable!`

prs.title: fix(linter/arrow-body-style): keep type assertions when adding a block body
prs.author: yan-almeida
prs.body:
Closes #27977

With `arrow-body-style: ["error", "always"]`, the fix unwrapped the concise body with `get_inner_expression`, which strips TS wrappers together with the parentheses, so the type assertion was lost. Now only the parentheses around the leading object literal are removed (the same tokens ESLint removes) and the rest of the expression is kept.

| Input | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `() => <T>{ id }` | `() => {return { id }}` | `() => {return <T>{ id }}` |
| `() => <T>({ id })` | `() => {return { id }}` | `() => {return <T>({ id })}` |
| `() => ({ id }) as T` | `() => {return { id }}` | `() => {return { id } as T}` |
| `() => ({ id }) satisfies T` | `() => {return { id }}` | `() => {return { id } satisfies T}` |

Plain `() => ({ id })` still becomes `() => {return { id }}`.

Tests: added a `.ts` test (`test_typescript`) with pass/fail/fix cases (also `({ id })!`, `(({ id }) as T)` and `requireReturnForObjectLiteral`) and its snapshot. `cargo test --all-features -p oxc_linter` and `just lint -p oxc_linter` pass.

AI disclosure: this PR was prepared with the help of an AI assistant (Claude).

prs.title: feat(ecmascript)!: fold surrogate strings with JSStr constants
prs.author: Dunqing
prs.body:
String constant evaluation used `Cow<str>`, so folds stopped at any string with a lone surrogate. `ConstantValue::String` now holds a `JSStr`, so these strings fold too, and results are built with `JSStrBuilder`, which joins surrogate halves the way the runtime does.

`indexOf`, `lastIndexOf`, `substring` and `slice` now share one UTF-16 code-unit implementation for every string. This also fixes miscompiles on main: `'éx'.indexOf('x')` folded to 2, `'abc'.indexOf('a', 4294967296)` to 0, `'abab'.lastIndexOf('b', NaN)` to -1, and `'abc'.substring(1, void 0)` to `''`. It includes #27097, which is closed.

String `concat` calls and chains fold into a template only when no argument with side effects follows one that may be an object, so `''.concat(a, (a.push(1), 'x'))` no longer becomes `` `${a}${(a.push(1), 'x')}` ``.

## Breaking changes

- `ConstantValue::String` holds `JSStr<'a>`, and `ConstantValue::into_string`, `evaluate_value_to_string` and `get_side_free_string_value` return `JSStr<'a>`.
- `StringIndexOf` and `StringLastIndexOf` take the search value as `JSStr` and use UTF-16 code unit positions.
- `StringSubstring` is removed.

Closes #15524. Closes #25158. Closes #26053. Based on #27096. Part of #26242. Continues #26759.

Implemented with AI assistance.

prs.title: fix(minifier,linter): keep `delete` of constant members and later JSX keys
prs.author: Dunqing
prs.body:
`delete "a"[0]`, `delete "a".length`, `delete [1].length` and `delete Number.NaN` delete a non-configurable property, so they are `false`, or a `TypeError` in strict mode. The minifier folded the member to its value first, and deleting a value is `true`:

```js
console.log(delete "😀"[0]); // false; minified to `console.log(!0)`
```

#27096 extended the string index fold to every string, so `delete "😀"[0]` became `!0` in 0.155.0. `delete "abc"[0]` and `delete "abc".length` were already wrong in 0.154.0. The member folds, the `Number.*` constant replacement and the `Number.NaN` normalization now skip the operand of `delete`. `delete obj["x"]` still becomes `delete obj.x`, and `delete Number["NaN"]` now minifies the same way every time.

`react/jsx-key` with `warnOnDuplicates` stopped at a template key with a substitution, `` key={`${a}`} ``, instead of reading the element's next `key`. Since #26717 the duplicate in `[<li key={`${a}`} key="dup" />, <li key={`${a}`} key="dup" />]` went unreported. The rule now falls through to the next `key` as 0.154.0 did.

Found by comparing 0.154.0 and 0.155.0 builds. Part of #26242.

Implemented with AI assistance.
